title: The Madoff Ponzi Scheme Explained Like You're 5
hook: He chaired the NASDAQ stock exchange three times -- and for almost fifty years quietly ran a fraud that paid old investors with money that was never actually invested.
body:
Bernie Madoff started a small trading firm in 1960 with $5,000 saved from lifeguarding. He became a pioneer of electronic trading and chaired the NASDAQ board three times -- while a separate, smaller arm of his firm, on its own floor, was paying old investors with new investors' cash and calling it a ten-percent annual return. A whistleblower named Harry Markopolos warned the SEC six separate times over nine years and was ignored. The 2008 crash finally broke it: clients asked for money that was not there, Madoff confessed to his own sons, and they turned him in. This is what the SEC's complaint, the guilty plea, and the sentencing record actually say happened.

For educational and entertainment purposes. Historical events are dramatised; no dialogue in this video is presented as a verbatim quotation except where directly attributed on screen.
pinned: The part that still gets me: the SEC looked at his firm eight separate times over sixteen years and never once called an outside bank to check a single trade. What number in this one surprised you most?
